e.etymology: A name of Hawaiian style ending in lani, heaven or sky. Name books gloss it as cheerful, but that meaning is hard to confirm in Hawaiian dictionaries.
A modern name of unclear source that fits the American family of names ending in -ir, such as Amir, Nasir and Zahir. Azir is also the emperor character in the game League of Legends.

assoc.t: Azir, the emperor champion in League of Legends

e.etymology: A recent American coinage in the sound family of Zaire and Kyaire. It has no established meaning.
An English rendering of the Welsh name Lloyd, from llwyd, gray or gray-haired. The Fl- spelling was an attempt to write the Welsh ll sound.

assoc.t: George Floyd, whose 2020 killing set off mass protests
Pink Floyd, the British rock band
Floyd the barber on The Andy Griffith Show

e.etymology: A spelling of Kylie, an Australian coinage possibly from kylie, a Noongar word for a boomerang, and also an Irish surname. Kylie spread worldwide with singer Kylie Minogue.
A spelling of Kaylee, a late 20th-century name that combines Kay and Lee and echoes the surnames Cayley and Keeley. Some families say this spelling like Callie.
e.note: Expect to be asked whether it is said KAY-lee or KAL-ee.

e.etymology: A transliteration of the Arabic name Iyad, from the root for supporting and strengthening. Iyad was also the name of an ancient Arab tribe.
A respelling of Naomi, from Hebrew No'omi, my pleasantness, from no'am, pleasantness. In the Bible Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth.

e.meaning: of Nairi, the ancient Armenian highlands
e.etymology: In Armenian, from Nairi, an Assyrian-era name for the Armenian highlands. Similar names occur elsewhere: Arabic Nayyira, shining, and Aymara nayra, eye, used in Latin America.
A modern American name in the family of Daylen, Dalton and Waylon. It has no meaning of its own.
An elaboration of Layla with a leading A, in the pattern of Alayna and Alaya. Layla is Arabic for night.
A 2000s American coinage that joins the Ky- of Kyle and Kyler to the -den ending of Aiden, Jayden and Kaden.
The Spanish Bible's spelling of Asahel, from Hebrew asah, to make, and El, God. Asahel was King David's nephew, a warrior said to run as fast as a gazelle.
The Anglicized form of Irish Órfhlaith, from ór, gold, and flaith, prince or sovereign. Brian Boru's sister bore it in the 10th century; in Denmark Orla is a man's name.
An English surname from Old English bucca, he-goat, and leah, woodland clearing. In Ireland Buckley also anglicizes Ó Buachalla, from buachaill, herdsman or boy.

assoc.t: surname of William F. Buckley Jr. and singer Jeff Buckley

e.etymology: A spelling of Greek Giannis, the everyday form of Ioannes (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. The spelling Yanis is especially popular in France and North Africa.
An Indian name usually connected with Sanskrit nihara, mist or dew, the root of the names Nihar and Niharika. Name lists give other meanings that are hard to confirm.
A spelling of Kaylee, a name coined toward the end of the 20th century from Kay and Lee, with an echo of the surnames Cayley and Keeley. Kaley is itself also a surname.
namesakes: Kaley Cuoco (Penny on The Big Bang Theory)

e.etymology: From Arabic jamil, beautiful or handsome. In the United States it has been used since the 1970s, chiefly in African American and Muslim families.
The Turkish word for sea, used as a name for both boys and girls and the most popular unisex name in Turkey. It is unrelated to Dennis.
e.note: Said deh-NEEZ, it sounds like Denise, which Americans know as a woman's name.

e.etymology: An American coinage that joins the popular Ja- beginning to the -laya sound of Alaya and Malaya.
A Spanish-influenced spelling of Kaylin, common in Central American families, with Key- writing the English sound of Kay. Kaylin itself combines Kay with the -lyn ending.
From Hebrew ayala, a doe or gazelle, among the top girls' names in Israel. Ayala is also a common Spanish surname of Basque origin and a separate Kazakh girls' name.
A transliteration of the Russian and Ukrainian spelling of Sophia, from Greek sophia, wisdom. The name spread through Christian Europe with the early saint Sophia.
From Sanskrit aradhya, one who is to be worshipped, from the verb aradh, to honor. It surged after Bollywood stars Aishwarya Rai and Abhishek Bachchan named their daughter Aaradhya in 2011.
In Arabic, kayan means existence or being and is given to girls and boys. A separate Persian name, also spelled Kayaan, recalls the legendary Kayanian kings of Iran.
A modern elaboration in the family of Aurelia and Ariella. The Aur- beginning traces to Latin aurum, gold, and -ella is a familiar feminine ending.
A spelling of Charlotte, the French feminine diminutive of Charles, from Germanic karl, free man. This form is often said with the stress on the second syllable, like Charlene.
An American coinage that combines Jay with the -von ending of Javon, Devon and Davon, used mainly in African American families since the 1990s.
A short form of Desiree, French for desired, and of the Spanish Desiderio, both from Latin desiderium, longing. Cuban bandleader Desi Arnaz of I Love Lucy made it familiar.
namesakes: Desi Arnaz (Cuban bandleader, Ricky Ricardo on I Love Lucy)

assoc.t: Desi Arnaz, Lucille Ball's husband and co-star
desi, a term for people and culture of South Asia

e.note: Desi is also the everyday word for people and things of South Asian origin.

e.etymology: A surname from a place name, traced to Old English fugol, bird, and tun, settlement. Americans knew it through steamboat builder Robert Fulton, and it peaked as a first name in the 1880s.
namesakes: Fulton Sheen (Catholic archbishop and 1950s television host)

assoc.t: Fulton County, Georgia, home to most of Atlanta
Fulton Street in Manhattan and Brooklyn

e.etymology: A respelling of Adley, a modern name that pairs the Ad- of Addison and Adeline with the -ley ending. Adley is also known from the children's YouTube channel A for Adley.
